ledger.x: c. 1350 BC: Aziru's Amurru. The Aziru page gives 'Reign: c. 35 regnal years c. 1350~1315 BC' and has him 'captured the city of Sumur'; Abdi-Ashirta, 'the first documented leader of Amurru', is only 'fl. 14th century BC' on his page, so the start is a bridging judgment at Aziru's accession. The infobox 'Established: c.…

c. 1350 BC: Amurru under Egyptian overlordship. The Amurru page has Aziru 'claimed to govern Amurru on Egypt's behalf' in the Amarna letters, while Akhenaten 'repeatedly asked Aziru to come to Egypt'; none of this is dated.
c. 1345 BC: Aziru leaves Egypt. 'He changed his allegiance to Suppiluliuma I around 1350-1345 BCE.'

c. 1345 BC: Amurru becomes a Hittite vassal. 'He changed his allegiance to Suppiluliuma I around 1350-1345 BCE'; the treaty is listed as 'Treaty of Suppiluliuma I with Aziru of Amurru (CTH 49)' with no year, and 'Amurru remained firmly in Hittite hands until the reign of the 19th Dynasty Pharaohs'. Mirrors the…
1274 BC: Egyptian influence over Amurru is lost after Kadesh.
1274 BC (bridged): Amurru is again a Hittite vassal.

c. 1200 BC: the Hittite vassalage ends. The page says references to Amurru 'disappear with the Hittite Empire and Ugarit'; the hittites dossier ends the vassalage in 1180, the page puts the kingdom's end 'circa 1200 BC'.

c. 1200 BC: Amurru ends in the Bronze Age collapse. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1200 BCE'; the kingdom ended 'during the Bronze Age Collapse circa 1200 BC'. The page names no successor (it mentions Middle Assyrian and Phrygian activity afterwards).

wars.name: Aziru's wars against Byblos
wars.outcome: Rib-Hadda of Byblos 'was ultimately exiled'; Aziru captured Sumur; Egypt summoned Aziru (EA 162) and detained him for 'at least a year'.

wars.name: Ramesses II's Amurru campaign and the Battle of Kadesh
wars.outcome: Ramesses II invades Amurru in year 4 (1275 BC) and fights Muwatalli II at Kadesh in May 1274 BC; he 'failed to retake Amurru and Qadesh'; Amurru stays in the Hittite sphere (disputed).

certainty.note: The page describes the land by features (coast, Akkar plains, Homs Gap), not a boundary.
